Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

several adjective and pronoun

also a few, a number of, quite a few, several days

classical

Ter. And. 3.3.2: aliquot mē adiērunt (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 7.18: aliquot epistulae (Lewis & Short)

aliquot

indeclinable numeral adjective

several, a few

A small number, not stated (Lewis & Short). With a word of time in the accusative, “for several …”: aliquot diēs.

Other words

  • complūrēs, complūra — several, a good many

    adjective, plural; gen. complūrium; neuter also complūria (mostly before Cicero) · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.8.2: complūrēs diēs (Lewis & Short); Sall. C. 23.4: complūribus narrāvit (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “more than one, not a few”, with no comparative force. As a noun, several people: complūribus narrāvit, she told several people.

  • plūrēs, plūra — several, more than one

    adjective, plural (the comparative of multī); gen. plūrium · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 5.6.23: circā sipunculī plūrēs

    Properly “more” (see more); without a comparison it is “a number of, several”.

Examples

  • aliquot mē adiērunt

    several people came to meTer. And. 3.3.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • ea complūribus narrāvit

    she told it to several peopleSall. C. 23.4 (Lewis & Short)

  • fonticulus in hōc, in fonte crātēr; circā sipunculī plūrēs miscent jūcundissimum murmur

    there is a little fountain here, a basin in the fountain, and round it several small jets mingle a most pleasant murmurPlin. Ep. 5.6.23

  • Aliquot diēs apud aviam manēbimus.

    We’ll stay at Grandma’s for a few days.composed

See also some, various.
